chunks: And it is not for any soul to die except by permission of Allah, as written in a decree. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give it from it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give it from it. And We will reward the grateful.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine decree and human desire in the context of death and reward?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia exegesis to establish the inevitability of death (al-Mawt) and the concept of 'ajal musamma' (appointed term), underscores that human agency is subordinate to Divine decree. It contrasts the transient nature of worldly desires with the eternal reward of the Hereafter, highlighting gratitude (shukr) as a key virtue for attaining divine favor. The mention of rewarding the grateful reinforces the Shia emphasis on active thankfulness as a means of spiritual elevation and divine proximity.
